description: cam init scaffolds a discoverable, commented [loop] section (meta_loop/worker_isolation/orch_context_window) in project.toml via a comment-capable TOML serializer.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed current signature is parse(input: string): object (used by parseToml in src/config/toml.ts). The reference page does not itself document comment handling, but Bun.TOML follows the TOML v1.0.0 spec, which mandates that '#' comment lines are ignored; US-001 pins this with an explicit test rather than trusting the doc.

userStories.title: Add comment emission to stringifyToml (parser stays comment-tolerant)
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need the TOML serializer to be able to emit '#' comment lines (and the parser to provably ignore them) so that cam init can scaffold self-documenting, commented config sections without breaking existing writes or round-trips.
acceptanceCriteria: stringifyToml (src/config/toml.ts:68-96) accepts an optional comments argument and can emit comment-only lines under a section header (a section that carries only commented example lines, no active keys). [oracle: grep -q 'comment' src/config/toml.ts]

Fully backward-compatible: when no comments are supplied, stringifyToml output is byte-identical to today and every existing serializer test in test/toml.test.ts passes unchanged. A new test asserts the no-comment path is unchanged. [oracle: bun test test/toml.test.ts]

The parser (parseToml / Bun.TOML.parse path) ignores '#' comment lines: parsing a project.toml that contains commented [loop] examples yields the same config object as the same file without them. A new test pins this (if Bun.TOML did not already skip comments, add tolerance). [oracle: bun test test/toml.test.ts]
Round-trip: parseToml(stringifyToml(config, comments)) deep-equals the config object (comments are non-semantic and do not appear as keys). Covered by a new test. [oracle: bun test test/toml.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/config/toml.ts (stringifyToml + stringifyScalar region), test/toml.test.ts. The comment feature MUST be opt-in: default (no comments) output byte-identical, because stringifyToml backs mergeIntoConfig which handles ALL project.toml writes (gotcha from issue). A comment-only [loop] block cannot be represented as an active key in TomlConfig (Record<string, scalar>), so the comment API must let the caller attach comment-only lines to a section header without pinning any key. Verify Bun.TOML.parse already skips '#' per TOML v1.0.0 (the toml.ts header already cites https://bun.com/reference/bun/TOML/parse); pin it with a test regardless. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard any array/regex access. Do NOT add a template file (issue gotcha).

userStories.title: cam init scaffolds a commented [loop] section in project.toml
userStories.description: As an operator running cam init, I need project.toml to contain a commented [loop] section documenting meta_loop, worker_isolation, and orch_context_window so that I discover these keys and their accepted values, without the scaffold pinning any active value (runtime read-with-default stays unchanged).
acceptanceCriteria: cam init (src/commands/setup.ts project.toml generation, ~661-683) emits a [loop] section containing COMMENTED example lines for meta_loop (accepted: auto | observe | off), worker_isolation (accepted: container | host), and orch_context_window (default 200000), using the US-001 comment support. [oracle: grep -qE '#.*meta_loop' <generated project.toml in test>]

The commented enums/defaults match the readers exactly and invent no values: meta_loop auto|observe|off (readMetaLoop, src/config/models.ts:236), worker_isolation container|host (readWorkerIsolation :301), orch_context_window default 200000 (DEFAULT_ORCH_CONTEXT_WINDOW :325). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The [loop] keys are COMMENTED examples, not active/pinned keys: a freshly scaffolded project.toml parses cleanly AND readMetaLoop/readWorkerIsolation/readOrchContextWindow return their code defaults (off / host / 200000) against it. A test scaffolds a fresh project.toml and asserts all three readers return defaults. [oracle: bun test]
The scaffolded file is valid parseable TOML (parseToml on the fresh scaffold does not throw and drops the comment lines). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/setup.ts (~661-683 mergeIntoConfig block), test under test/ mirroring setup/toml. GOTCHA: cam init calls mergeIntoConfig multiple times (models/issue_system/ship/plan, then notify) and each call re-parses+re-serializes, which strips comments (comments are non-semantic). Emit the commented [loop] block on a write path that survives: e.g. append the [loop] comment block on a single dedicated/final write, and make it idempotent, so subsequent mergeIntoConfig calls don't duplicate or lose it. Do NOT emit uncommented keys like meta_loop = "observe" (that pins the value and defeats read-with-default in src/config/models.ts). Do NOT introduce a separate project.toml template file (issue gotcha). This is the cam init scaffold for downstream projects; cam-cli's own scripts/cam/project.toml is CAM-277 (out of scope).
